title: Alternating GenAI and non-GenAI ethical-framework analysis
summary: Pairs research an assigned ethical framework and a current computing event through stages that explicitly alternate between AI-required and AI-prohibited work. They compare stakeholder analyses and scenarios, evaluate AI omissions and additions, and submit the complete ChatGPT dialogue.

sources.title: WIP: Generative AI as an Instructional Resource in a Computer Science Ethics Course

locator.section: III. Methodology, A. Assignment Design and Integration

sources.evidence_quote: Groups were then asked to complete a series of exercises outside of class that alternated between requiring the use of Gen AI and prohibiting the use of Gen AI.

assessment.summary: Apply an ethical framework and stakeholder analysis manually and with ChatGPT, then compare and evaluate the results.
student_actions: Prompt ChatGPT for a summary of an assigned ethical framework.
Create a hypothetical scenario and stakeholder list without AI.
Generate and refine an AI scenario with edge cases and legal effects.
Find and summarize a recent computing-related news event without AI.
Compare manual and AI stakeholder analyses.

student_role.description: Permission changes by stage: ChatGPT 3.5 is required for designated activities and prohibited for the paired manual activities.

prohibited_actions: Using GenAI to create the student-authored scenario, article summary, or initial stakeholder analysis

grading.method: Rubric-based grading emphasizing a systematic prompt strategy; detailed weights are not reported.

reported_results: Twelve of thirteen groups identified stakeholders supplied only by GenAI and stakeholders identified only by the group.

provenance.extraction_method: Full PDF read from pdftotext output.
